entries.title: Almost isn’t good enough for Pete Crow-Armstrong, but his career as Cubs’ centerpiece is just starting
entries.summary: <p>SAN DIEGO — Pete Crow-Armstrong’s begrudging retreat back to the dugout was the last “almost” in a night full of them.</p><p>He had almost checked his swing, but was ruled, for the second consecutive time, to have struck out by the third-base ump.</p><p>Many innings prior, he had almost robbed Fernando Tatis Jr. of a tone-setting leadoff homer. Along the way, he almost got the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ silenced bats going by walking and stealing a base.</p><p>This isn’t horseshoes. This isn’t hand grenades. Tuesday, all that “almost” amounted to a blowout playoff loss.</p><p>“Almost” doesn’t cut it, and Crow-Armstrong — upset enough by what doesn’t go right that he lamented getting picked off <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/15/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-hit-for-cycle-walk-off-win-rockies-pedro-ramirez-matt-shaw-shota-imanaga" >the night he hit for the cycle in a walk-off Cubs win</a> — has reminded everyone of that all summer long.</p><p>“When the ultimate goal is to win every ballgame you step out on the field for,” he said that night back in June, “it’s really easy to highlight the stuff that you’re not so happy about that you’ve got to make sure never happens again.”</p><p>But the truth is that even in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/29/cubs-padres-game-1-loss-matthew-boyd-home-runs-fernando-tatis-manny-machado-playoffs-mlb-postseason-wild-card-series" >a crucial game where nothing went the Cubs’ way</a>, there were still those glimpses of the type of impact Crow-Armstrong — and only Crow-Armstrong — is capable of making, the impact that has made him the runaway favorite to win the MVP.</p><p>He didn’t show off the kind of power that led to a league-leading 45 homers, securing <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/24/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-40-40-season-club-mlb-history-matthew-boyd-kevin-gausman-red-sox-doubleheader" >the seventh 40-40 in baseball history</a>. But he flashed his defensive ability. He flashed his base-running ability. It’s that stuff that makes him the one-of-a-kind player the Cubs marveled at this season.</p><p>“What’s so great about his game is he can not homer this series or whatever and still be the best player on the field,” second baseman Nico Hoerner said Tuesday. “It’s amazing that he led baseball in homers and he can still dominate without hitting homers.”</p><p>And it’s all that stuff that makes him the player Cubs fans will watch make a game-changing impact for years to come. The Cubs locked Crow-Armstrong up on a long-term contract earlier this year, making him the unquestioned centerpiece of both the present and future.</p><p>There was another “almost” Tuesday, maybe, Crow-Armstrong perhaps almost getting ejected as he griped about the second check-swing call to the ump who made it.</p><p>The Cubs — who see <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/26/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-balk-umpires-diamondbacks-eduardo-rodriguez-craig-counsell-matthew-boyd" >those displays of emotion</a> as part of what makes Crow-Armstrong who he is — have no desire to see them go away.</p><p>“I love the way he just wears his heart on his sleeve and doesn’t try to control, sometimes, his anger,” designated hitter Michael Conforto said a couple weeks ago. “As long as he doesn’t hurt himself. It’s part of the reason he’s so great.”</p><p>Changes in mindset, though, have been just as important as changes in what he does at the plate as Crow-Armstrong has evolved from someone who could be an important part of the Cubs’ future into the player in the middle of everything.</p><p>In part, he has his manager to thank.</p><p>“[Craig Counsell has] changed the way that I operate off the field a lot this year,” Crow-Armstrong said last week. “He’s just encouraged me to find a lot of enjoyment outside of coming to the field every day, which is something that was hard for me in years past.</p><p>“I have a hard time turning off baseball brain. He’s just been hugely influential in terms of getting me to show up in the right headspace. I credit a ton of my success this year to that and to him.”</p><p>Remember, too, that Crow-Armstrong is only 24 years old. He’s made an enormous leap from last season to this season.</p><p>What leaps could follow?</p><p>“There’s definitely room for him to grow,” first baseman Michael Busch said Wednesday. “He’s just tapping into becoming an extremely good player, a superstar in this league, and him being the person that he is, he’s going to continue to work and he’s going to look for that opportunity to grow. It’s No. 1 on the list of why he’s going to continue to get better over the next several years.”</p><p>So you’re saying this might not even be the fully formed version of the best player in baseball?</p><p>Maybe almost.</p>

entries.title: Des Plaines police release video of officer fatally shooting 21-year-old man last month
entries.summary: <p>Des Plaines police have released <a class="Link" href="https://www.desplainesil.gov/Residents/News/Des-Plaines-Police-Release-Video-Audio-Recordings-of-the-Officer-Involved-Shooting?fbclid=IwY2xjawUqcOtleHRuA2FlbQIxMABwZG9mAWJyaWQRMWF0MDUySEFUTktVMllGeUpzcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEenhGaFYJkQwbdWHxNBJsy292F4H63fPCH7SuWKp-3nXqwW18_ijHgAOCsxDc_aem_EejRMCVevDY377wxR0K9hQ" target="_blank" ><u>audio and video footage</u></a> of the moments leading up to an officer fatally shooting a man last month who was walking toward him with an electric hedge trimmer.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/17/six-des-plaines-cops-including-officer-who-fired-deadly-shots-at-man-21-placed-on-administrative-leave" target="_blank" ><u>Six officers were placed on temporary paid administrative leave</u></a> by the Des Plaines Department in connection with the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/09/des-plaines-police-officer-shoots-man-while-responding-to-domestic-disturbance" target="_blank" ><u>fatal shooting of Ayham Babidi</u></a>, 21, on Sept. 9 about 2:30 p.m. at 2047 E. Touhy Ave., which is a standard procedure during active use-of-force investigations.</p><p>In a 911 call also released alongside the footage, Babidi’s mother is heard requesting a police response and an ambulance after Babidi had allegedly threatened to kill her during a mental health episode. A bystander’s cell phone video shows Babidi breaking a window at his own home with an unplugged wired electric hedge trimmer and walking around the front yard.</p><p>Police dash cam footage shows Babidi walking with the hedge trimmer and telling an officer he followed to drop his gun as Sgt. Matthew Muchow, stationed nearby, instructs Babidi to drop the device. </p><p>“Show me your hands,” Muchow, who has been with the department for 22 years, is heard saying as he exits his squad car. </p><p>“I’m not gonna put it down, you’re gonna put it down,” Babidi responds.</p><p>Babidi exits the frame of the dashcam video, and two gunshots are heard in succession, followed by a pause and then a third shot. Police said Muchow and other first responders tried to render aid to Babidi before he was taken to a nearby hospital where he died.</p><p>Muchow had activated his body camera before getting out of the squad car but <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/10/des-plaines-police-said-cop-body-camera-wasnt-on-when-21-year-old-with-hedge-trimmer-was-shot" target="_blank" ><u>didn’t turn it on when he got out</u></a>, meaning the moments when he walked backward across Touhy Avenue and shot Babidi three times were captured from a distance on a neighbor’s security camera. The video, however, is largely obscured by a tree.</p><p>The Major Case Assistance Team — a multijurisdictional law enforcement group — is investigating the shooting and Muchow’s use of force. The Cook County state’s attorney’s office will review that investigation, Des Plaines police said.</p><p>Des Plaines police also said an independent investigator will be hired to review departmental policies and procedures related to the shooting.</p><p>“Any loss of life is a tragedy, and we recognize the profound grief this incident brings to those affected,” the department said in a statement. “Our thoughts are with the family as they process this event, and we remain committed to a transparent investigative process conducted in partnership with MCAT and the Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office.”</p>

entries.title: White Sox keep their surprising season going with wild-card series sweep in Houston
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — Early in this improbable <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> season, hitting coach Derek Shomon had a thought about second baseman Chase Meidroth that seemed bold but now seems sage.</p><p>‘‘[Assistant hitting coach] Joel [McKeithan] and I were like, ‘Dude, you can probably hit 15 or 20 [home runs] this year,’ ’’ Shomon said.</p><p>After Meidroth launched a backbreaking, three-run shot in sixth inning of the Sox’ 7-3 victory against the Astros that completed a two-game sweep in the American League wild-card series, the 5-9 infielder is at 17 and counting.</p><p>‘‘I knew I got it,’’ a beer- and champagne-drenched Meidroth said in the visitors’ locker room. ‘‘It’s a moment you dream about as a kid, coming through for your team like that in a big moment.’’</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="113" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/QGHnTxkaVnM?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="The White Sox celebrate their wild-card series win over the Astros"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>Earlier in the at-bat, manager Will Venable had Meidroth trying to lay down a bunt to push the two runners over, a more typical ask of the once-contact-oriented hitter. But Meidroth and the Sox showed throughout the sweep that they’re capable of more than anyone anticipated.</p><p>‘‘This just shows the resilience of our team,’’ starting pitcher Sean Burke said. ‘‘We show up no matter who were playing, no matter where we’re at. Doesn’t matter if we’re up or not, we play winning baseball.’’</p><p>In the two games at Daikin Park, the Sox were ahead throughout. They scored in the first inning of each game and turned the home crowd into boo-birds with an energetic brand of play that forced defensive mistakes from what was supposed to be a battle-tested opponent with more experience.</p><p>‘‘Sammy [Antonacci] setting the tone was really indicative of that fearlessness, and the guys responded behind him,’’ Venable said of his rookie leadoff man, who scored twice and drove in two runs in his first playoff action.</p><p>When three solo homers by the Astros against Burke narrowed the Sox’ advantage to 4-3, Venable conceded after the game that the momentum had switched to the opposition. But while they weren’t given postseason starts, well-traveled veterans Anthony Kay and Eric Fedde got the biggest outs of the day.</p><p>Kay induced fly outs from AL MVP favorite Yordan Alvarez and Jose Altuve to strand the potential go-ahead runs in the fifth, and Fedde — after pitching for the historically awful 2024 Sox — worked the final two innings to punch the South Siders’ ticket to the AL Division Series against the Guardians.</p><p>‘‘I’m so glad they chose me with the ball and to give the team the win this whole fan base deserved, this whole organization deserved,’’ Fedde said.</p><p>It was deserved, but even the architects of this turnaround would admit it arrived early.</p><p>‘‘Did I expect it to happen this quickly and be where we’re at in this journey?’’ general manager Chris Getz said. ‘‘No, I didn’t.’’</p><p>No MLB team in history had made the playoffs after two consecutive seasons of 100 losses or more, let alone three. To add a playoff-series victory — the Sox’ first since 2005 — on top of it was enough to draw chairman Jerry Reinsdorf into a jubilant clubhouse.</p><p>‘‘I didn’t think it would come to fruition this fast,’’ Reinsdorf said. ‘‘I really thought 2027 was the year that we would contend.’’</p><p>Next comes a showdown against the Guardians, whom the Sox have battled all season. The Sox won the season series 7-6 but lost the AL Central race to them by a game. At this point, the Sox have every reason to set their sights on the whole thing.</p><p>‘‘We’ve seen crazier things,’’ shortstop Colson Montgomery said about reaching the World Series. ‘‘All that matters is being hot right now, and we’re hot.’’</p><p>A winning clubhouse is no place to curb ambition, and with the way the Sox are feeling, they’re only headed to bigger and better things. That includes Meidroth, too.</p><p>‘‘Chase can win a batting title,’’ Shomon said.</p><p></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/chicago-white-sox-manager-will-venable-general-manager-chris-getz-chairman-jerry-reinsdorf-jin-wong-houston-astros-cleveland-guardians-mlb-playoffs-postseason" >Will Venable deserves lots of credit for White Sox’ success, but he won’t take it</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/white-sox-complete-wild-card-series-sweep-over-astros-setting-up-alds-matchup-with-guardians" >White Sox complete wild-card series sweep over Astros, setting up ALDS matchup with Guardians</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Will Venable deserves lots of credit for White Sox' success, but he won't take it
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — Whenever <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> manager Will Venable is asked about himself, he rarely answers about himself.</p><p>When asked what makes this Sox team different from recent, less successful iterations, he said, ‘‘It starts with Chris Getz,’’ the general manager.</p><p>When asked how he has handled his first postseason as a manager, he said, ‘‘I feel really well-supported [and] that’s really a credit to my staff.’’</p><p>Certainly, Venable deserves credit for guiding a team to the playoffs after three consecutive seasons with more than 100 losses — something that never had happened in major-league history. But he never will accept it.</p><p>He happily will take a spot in the American League Division Series against the Guardians instead. That’s where the Sox are headed after beating the Astros 7-3 on Wednesday to win the wild-card series 2-0, keeping a stunning season alive.</p><p>‘‘He’s built for this,’’ Getz said while trying to stay clear of the beer and champagne showers in the clubhouse. ‘‘His leadership ability, his competency, his ability to communicate with players, his temperament — he really is made for this.’’</p><p>Getz hired Venable, the son of former major-league outfielder Max Venable, but never dreamed he could turn the Sox into a playoff team — let alone a playoff-series-winning team — in such a short time. But he said he did know that Venable would be the perfect partner in that pursuit.</p><p>‘‘When it comes to Will Venable, so many people want him to succeed,’’ Getz said, still managing to stay dry. ‘‘It’s how he treats people. It could be anyone in the building. I just knew that he was going to be able to get a team and an organization to pull toward something special.’’</p><p>‘‘Will’s obviously done a fabulous job,’’ chairman Jerry Reinsdorf said outside the raucous clubhouse. ‘‘He taught these guys how to win.’’</p><p>He did more than that. With Getz’s help, he assembled a coaching staff in which he has complete faith. The players are the ones making it happen, but Venable’s staff is helping them make it happen.</p><p>‘‘He empowers his players; he empowers his staff,’’ assistant GM Jin Wong told the Sun-Times. ‘‘That’s very important from a leadership perspective. It’s less about doing than empowering the people you put in place. That creates an environment that is very trusting.’’</p><p>It sounds antithetical, but part of being a leader is allowing others to lead. Delegating is one of Venable’s strengths, and his coaches largely have repaid that trust. He’s more than happy to point that out.</p><p>‘‘If you have somebody in those types of leadership positions that doesn’t need all the credit and spreads the credit around, it makes people feel good, props them up,’’ Wong said. ‘‘That goes a long way.’’</p><p>Venable is, in a word, impressive. Yes, he has made mistakes, particularly when he made a second mound visit in the first inning of a game in August, requiring him to pull Noah Schultz. But he took responsibility, and that’s what his players do. They follow his lead.</p><p>‘‘He’s got this air about him that is calm and collected,’’ Wong said. ‘‘He’s very approachable. He’s one of those guys you look up to. He’s a great example of leadership.’’</p><p>It’s a different environment than the Sox experienced under previous managers. Since letting World Series-winning manager Ozzie Guillen go at the end of the 2011 season, the Sox had struggled to find a good fit.</p><p>Robin Ventura managed for five nondescript seasons, the first of which was his best with an 85-77 record. He didn’t exactly push for the job, but he took it. Rick Renteria followed with four mostly forgettable seasons, the last of which resulted in a wild-card berth. However, managing for his job, Renteria mismanaged that series, and the Sox showed him the door.</p><p>After the highly regarded A.J. Hinch became available after his one-year suspension for the 2017 Astros’ sign-stealing scandal, the Sox were so smitten with him that they never even interviewed him. Reinsdorf much preferred to right a wrong from almost 35 years before and bring back then 76-year-old Tony La Russa, whom Reinsdorf had fired in 1986.</p><p>Granted, La Russa led the Sox to a division title in 2021, but the ’22 team — not to mention the overall La Russa experience — was a profound disappointment. That led to even more disappointment under Pedro Grifol, which led to Reinsdorf cleaning house. He fired president Kenny Williams and GM Rick Hahn and put Getz in charge of everything.</p><p>Getz hired Venable. Two seasons later, the Sox not only made the postseason, but they won a series. They hadn’t done that since sweeping the Astros in the 2005 World Series — in Houston, of all places.</p><p>Now it’s off to Cleveland. Whether the Guardians stole the Central from the Sox’ grasp in the last two weeks of the season or whether the Sox handed it to them is debatable. But it won’t matter one bit if the Sox beat them in the ALDS, moving one step closer to the unfathomable: a spot in the World Series.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/white-sox-keep-their-surprising-season-going-with-wild-card-series-sweep-in-houston-chase-meidroth-jerry-reinsdorf-chris-getz-will-venable-colson-montgomery-erick-fedde" >White Sox keep their surprising season going with wild-card series sweep in Houston</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/white-sox-complete-wild-card-series-sweep-over-astros-setting-up-alds-matchup-with-guardians" >White Sox complete wild-card series sweep over Astros, setting up ALDS matchup with Guardians</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Were 2026 Cubs 'drawn up' to be a World Series team? If so, it's hard to see it
entries.summary: <p>SAN DIEGO — A tall, slender, blue-clad <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> supporter stepped onto an elevator headed down from the suite level after watching his favorite team get demolished 8-0 by the Padres in Game 1 of a best-of-three wild-card series at Petco Park.</p><p>Wearing a grim expression, he shook his head and offered, “Well, that’s not how you draw it up.”</p><p>A gaggle of reporters on their way down to the home and visiting clubhouses seemed to appreciate the well-delivered deadpan.</p><p>Comedic stylings notwithstanding, Cubs chairman Tom Ricketts was exactly right — and in more ways than one.</p><p>No, indeed, having Matthew Boyd surrender a home run to Fernando Tatis Jr. on his first pitch of the night wasn’t part of the game plan. Watching Tatis and Manny Machado whip a gold-towel-waving crowd into a thunderous frenzy before the Cubs even woke up and rubbed the regular season out of their eyes wasn’t high on the agenda. Cubs hitters flailing at balls out of the strike zone and making soft contact like it was their first swings of batting practice wasn’t on the ol’ to-do list.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">It’s me and <a href="https://x.com/SLGreenberg?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@SLGreenberg</a> from San Diego ahead of Game 1 of the Cubs’ playoff series against the Padres. Stay classy, folks. <a href="https://t.co/n0VVXKs5Eg">pic.twitter.com/n0VVXKs5Eg</a></p>— Vinnie Duber (@VinnieDuber) <a href="https://x.com/VinnieDuber/status/2105061912858001753?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 29, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Or as Cubs manager Craig Counsell perfectly put it, “They had a lot to cheer about tonight, and we didn’t give them anything to be quiet about.”</p><p>But even though Ricketts wasn’t getting at this and might disagree strongly with it, he spoke truth in another, broader sense: These Cubs probably aren’t how you draw up a true World Series contender.</p><p>Going back further than that, the Cubs probably haven’t been drawn up to win it all since Theo Epstein was in charge.</p><p>With the Cubs in a second straight postseason without there being a clear sense of a pitching rotation — who, when, why — it really drives home just how far we are from the 2016 scenario in which then-manager Joe Maddon, along with Epstein and then-general manager Jed Hoyer, decided to leave a 15-game winner, Jason Hammel, off the roster for every stage of the playoffs en route to a World Series championship.</p><p>When you have stone-cold aces Jon Lester and Jake Arrieta to throw at an opponent — any opponent — you know in your bones you can win. Kyle Hendricks was baseball’s ERA leader. John Lackey had won World Series-clinching games with both the Angels and the Red Sox.</p><p>Lackey was far from that team’s best starter, but he was a clear choice over Hammel because he’d been through the wars, still oozed fearlessness and was so respected. It’s oversimplifying it a bit, but he was that team’s Kevin Gausman, the been-there, done-that veteran the Cubs turned to Wednesday in a must-win Game 2 against the Padres. Only, Lackey’s October track record was better than Gausman’s, whose previous teams lost five of the last seven playoff games in which he started. Lackey surely would’ve been this Cubs team’s Game 1 guy.</p><p>Hoyer, now in charge, received a lot of credit for signing third baseman Alex Bregman, who had an outstanding first season with the Cubs, and for acquiring quality starters Gausman and Clay Holmes at the trade deadline. Hoyer also made a good trade for starter David Peterson in June, when the team was desperate for help.</p><p>But the Cubs went into the playoffs without a true ace or even a starter — any starter — in whom they could believe wholeheartedly. That’s not how you draw it up, nor is assembling a bullpen year after year guided by the conceit that the Cubs will make it work well just because they’re, you know, the Cubs. Hoyer need only see the electric, almost unhittable back end of the Padres’ bullpen for the way to draw it up.</p><p>There’s also the issue of player payroll, and on this front it’s always hard to know where blaming Ricketts alone should stop and assigning some of the blame to the conservative Hoyer should begin. Remember, this Cubs front office has made it clear its aim is to be good enough to get into the playoff field every year. Not to rip off 100 wins. Not to cut through the competition like a chain saw. Not to overtake the Brewers and win the division, whatever it takes. No, the Cubs just want to give themselves a chance because, gee whiz, anything can happen in October.</p><p>When Epstein was at the wheel, the Cubs simply spent more than they do now relative to the rest of the league. Four times from 2016 to 2020, Epstein’s last season, they ranked in the top five in payroll. On Hoyer’s watch, the highest any of the six teams have ranked in spending is seventh (in 2024 and 2026). If the Cubs don’t seem to be of World Series caliber to you, right there is one of the clearest reasons.</p><p>Maybe Ricketts believed in Epstein — a superstar exec — just a bit more. Maybe ownership got its World Series and lost the sense of urgency to do more than rake in revenue.</p><p>It’s hard to say.</p><p>But the rest isn’t hard to see.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/30/padres-cubs-fernando-tatis-manny-machado-xander-bogaerts-pete-crow-armstrong-alex-bregman-mlb-postseason" >Padres’ superstars show Cubs how it’s done in Game 1 rout</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/30/cubs-game-2-playoff-starter-starting-pitcher-kevin-gausman-wild-card-series-mlb-postseason" >Facing elimination, Cubs starting playoff-tested Kevin Gausman in Game 2 vs. Padres</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/30/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-mvp-playoffs-game-1-game-2-padres-wild-card-series-mlb-postseason" target="_blank" >Almost isn’t good enough for Pete Crow-Armstrong, but his career as Cubs’ centerpiece is just starting</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Man charged with attempted murder in 2025 Austin shooting
entries.summary: <p>A man is facing attempted murder charges in connection with the shooting of a 45-year-old man in Austin last November, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Juan Rodriguez, 23, was charged following his arrest on Tuesday with attempted first-degree murder, three counts of aggravated battery for discharging a firearm, causing great bodily harm and using a deadly weapon, police said.</p><p>The shooting victim was standing on the sidewalk in the 700 block of North Leamington Avenue at 1:20 p.m. on Nov. 28, 2025, when Rodriguez allegedly shot him from inside a green truck, police said. </p><p>The wounded man was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital in critical condition.</p><p>Rodriguez is due in court for a detention hearing Thursday.</p>

entries.summary: <p>The girls flag football team at North Lawndale College Prep headed into the playoffs with a big boost from the Chicago Bears.</p><p>The team surprised the Lady Phoenix with a dolly full of brand-new equipment: cleats, pads, helmets, sports bras and more.</p><p>“We really thought we [were] in trouble at first,” junior Emily Goodman said. “Now, actually everybody is happy. entries.title: 2 hospitalized after being shot on CTA bus
entries.summary: <p>Two people were shot while riding on a CTA bus in Englewood Wednesday afternoon, according to Chicago police.</p><p>A woman, 65, and a man, 57, were both on the bus in the 300 block of West 63rd Street at 4:40 p.m. when they were shot, police said.</p><p>The man, who suffered a single gunshot wound to his upper body, was taken to University of Chicago Medical Center in critical condition. The woman, struck in her left arm, was transported to the same hospital in fair condition, police said.</p><p>Police did not disclose whether the person who shot them was on the bus at the time, or fired into the bus from outside.</p><p>No one is in custody.</p>

entries.title: White Sox complete wild-card series sweep over Astros, setting up ALDS matchup with Guardians
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — Led by Chase Meidroth’s three-run blast in the sixth inning, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> defeated the American League West champion Astros 7-3, sweeping their best-of-three wild card series and setting up a Division Series showdown with the rival Cleveland Guardians beginning this weekend.</p><p>For the second-straight evening at Daikin Park, the young Sox had Astros fans turning on their team early.</p><p>After being flummoxed by Houston ace Hunter Brown twice in the regular season, the Sox hung a four-spot on the former American League Cy Young finalist. His departure accelerated by balky defense–two errors on top of Yordan Alvarez failing to reel in Sam Antonacci’s leadoff double to the left-center gap–Brown walked off to boos after two outs and 36 pitches.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="113" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/QGHnTxkaVnM?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="The White Sox celebrate their wild-card series win over the Astros"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>But for the second-straight evening, an early Sox lead didn’t equate to a killshot. After his own first inning hit the rocks early in Game 1, Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh came on and stopped the bleeding by getting Antonacci to ground out with the bases loaded. His efforts, and three gutty–and initially scoreless–innings from Peter Lambert pitching on two days rest, set the stage for the Astros to walk down the early deficit with three solo shots off Sox starter Sean Burke in his four innings of work.</p><p>As it turns out, the killshot simply had to wait until the sixth, when Lambert was at the end of his rope. Andrew Benintendi and Tristan Peters led off the innings with walks, bringing on Bryan Abreu for his second outing in as many days. Abreu got eight outs and struck out six. But on his first batter of the game, he hung a 3-1 slider that Meidroth obliterated to left field, roaring with delight immediately upon contact.</p><p>The extra margin allowed the Sox to close out the final four innings with spectacular work from Jordan Hicks, who struck out three in two perfect frames, and Erick Fedde. After being a rare bright spot in a record-setting 121-loss season, the 33-year-old starter got to be on the mound to seal a turnaround of which he so desperately wanted to be a part.</p><p></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/chicago-white-sox-manager-will-venable-general-manager-chris-getz-chairman-jerry-reinsdorf-jin-wong-houston-astros-cleveland-guardians-mlb-playoffs-postseason" >Will Venable deserves lots of credit for White Sox’ success, but he won’t take it</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/white-sox-keep-their-surprising-season-going-with-wild-card-series-sweep-in-houston-chase-meidroth-jerry-reinsdorf-chris-getz-will-venable-colson-montgomery-erick-fedde" >White Sox keep their surprising season going with wild-card series sweep in Houston</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Bears report: CB Kyler Gordon returns to practice
entries.summary: <p>What happened Wednesday at Halas Hall:</p><h3><b>Gordon back at practice</b></h3><p>Kyler Gordon, who hurt his calf this spring and hasn't practiced since, participated in full in Wednesday's walk-through, opening a 21-day window for the slot cornerback to return to game action from the physically-unable-to-perform list. Gordon cannot play in a game until Week 5; if he's not activated by Oct. 20, he'll be lost for the season.</p><p>Gordon's calf injury has been a major source of frustration from his bosses inside Halas Hall, with coach Ben Johnson often giving terse, monosyllabic answers when pressed for updates. He rehabbed the injury both inside and outside the facility in recent weeks. Still, Gordon has rarely practiced or played since he signed a contract extension in April 2025. He appeared in three games last season and went to IR twice because of various soft-tissue maladies.</p><h3><b>Jones ‘week-to-week’</b></h3><p>Left tackle Theo Benedet figures to start this week against the Jets after Johnson called Braxton Jones "week-to-week" with a knee injury suffered Monday. He would not have participated had the Bears held a full practice, according to the team's esetimated injury report. Neither would guard Jonah Jackson (personal), while safety Cam Lewis was limited with a hip problem.</p><p>As for Benedet's backup, Johnson suggested that the team could use Jordan McFadden or even star guard Joe Thuney in a pinch. Ozzy Trapilo is still working his way back from a patellar tendon injury.</p><h3>Dexter gets paid</h3><p>Exactly one month after the Bears traded him to the Falcons because he'd fallen out of their rotation, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter signed a four-year, $78 million contract extension. He was playing the last season of his rookie deal.<br></p>

entries.title: Cubs don’t get close to meeting championship expectations as season ends in two-game playoff sweep vs. Padres
entries.summary: <p>SAN DIEGO — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ season is over, ending with a two-game thud.</p><p>This wasn’t how it was supposed to end, certainly not this early, not this quickly.</p><p>But the World Series hopes the Cubs held since the spring were officially dashed Wednesday night in Southern California, the team looking far from championship-caliber for a second straight game as they were swept out of the playoffs with a 4-1 loss to the Padres.</p><p>The Padres came into the series red hot. The Cubs didn’t, losers of four of their final six games in the regular season and struggling to score in the cold, windy conditions at Wrigley Field and Fenway Park.</p><p>A scene change to the picture-perfect weather of San Diego didn’t do anything to awaken their bats, though, and a night after they were shut out — with Padres starter Michael King taking a no-hit bid into the seventh inning — they were mostly kept off home plate again, limited to just five hits after mustering only three in Game 1.</p><p>All told, the regular season’s highest-scoring team scored just 16 runs in the last eight games it played in 2026.</p><p>Though the offensive troubles were undoubtedly a team-wide issue, it was hard to escape the failings of the Cubs’ two best hitters, Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman, who were hitless in the two-game series, going 0-for-15 and striking out eight times.</p><p>That obviously paled in comparison to what the Padres’ dynamic duo of Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado did in Game 1, each homering off lefty Matthew Boyd in the first inning of that contest and scoring five of their team’s eight runs.</p><p>The Cubs tabbed righty Kevin Gausman with their season on the line Wednesday, to little better result. Bothered by a balky left shoulder the last week, he lasted 3⅓ innings, giving up a pair of runs after allowing three hits to start the bottom of the second inning.</p><p>But the biggest blow came right after he exited in the fourth, chased by a one-out double. Righty reliever Daniel Palencia — who didn’t allow a run in his last eight appearances in the regular season — followed up a strikeout by giving up a two-out, two-run homer to pinch-hitter Gavin Sheets that sent Petco Park into a frenzy.</p><p>The Cubs’ lineup — which squandered a couple early chances, stranding five runners in the third and fourth innings — was even quieter from there against the Padres’ mighty bullpen, putting just three men on base in the final five innings.</p><p>And that was that, a season in the books without much resistance to a San Diego steamroller that looks like the sort of championship-capable team the Cubs believed they were all summer long.</p><p>The numbers said they were, too. They led the majors in runs scored. They had, far and away, the best defense in the sport. And Crow-Armstrong, the presumptive MVP, had an all-time campaign, joining baseball’s exclusive 40-40 club and playing Gold Glove defense in center field.</p><p>But the Cubs picked the wrong time to go into hibernation, what they hoped would be a run deep into October not even reaching that month on the calendar.</p><p>Last season’s playoff exit, in the NLDS at the hands of the rival Brewers, struck as an early one. But by comparison, it was a lengthy stay.</p><p>After losing the division race to the Brewers last year by five games, they finished a whopping 14 games behind their rivals this year. After beating these Padres in the opening playoff round in 2025 and taking the Brewers to five games, they managed to appear in only two postseason bouts in 2026, losing both.</p><p>Inarguably, a disappointing step backward for an organization with big expectations and little playoff success to show for them.</p>

entries.title: Victorious White Sox escape Peacock, advance to TBS, truTV
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — White Sox fans, your TV nightmare is over. For as long as the Sox are alive in the postseason, their games will no longer be relegated to a streaming service or an under-distributed cable channel.</p><p>Having vanquished the Astros, the Sox now face the rival Guardians in the American League Division Series, which will air entirely on cable channels TBS and truTV, plus streaming service HBO Max.</p><p>But never mind the streamer. TBS and truTV are available on practically every cable and satellite provider. Do you know where they aren’t available? Oddly enough, Fubo, one of three platforms that carries NBC Sports Network, which aired the Sox-Astros series, though most people likely watched it on Peacock.</p><p>That isn’t Sox fans’ problem anymore. Game 1 of the best-of-five series is scheduled for noon Saturday in Cleveland. Game 2 is set for 4 p.m. Monday. The rest of the series schedule will be revealed later.</p><p>As for the rest of the wild-card round, with the Cubs and Red Sox joining the Astros in elimination land, only the Phillies-Braves series reached Game 3. That will air at 7 p.m. Thursday on NBC and, of course, Peacock.</p>

entries.title: White Sox chairman Jerry Reinsdorf celebrates 'gratifying' wild-card series victory
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — Three years ago, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> chairman <b>Jerry Reinsdorf</b> named <b>Chris Getz</b> his new general manager and was criticized on two fronts.</p><p>‘‘I lived up to the faith you guys all had in me when I hired Chris,’’ Reinsdorf quipped inside a victorious Sox locker room Wednesday at Daikin Park. ‘‘Happy we vindicated your judgment in praising me for hiring him.’’</p><p>The first issue was that Reinsdorf promoted Getz from within without formally interviewing outside candidates, which didn’t exactly seem like the cure to the insularity that had troubled previous Sox front offices.</p><p>‘‘As an analogy, one of the worst things that can happen when you are house-hunting is to find the best house first, and you keep on going and somebody else bought the house,’’ Reinsdorf said. ‘‘I realized I had the guy. I didn’t want to go beyond that.’’</p><p>The second was that at Getz’s introductory news conference, Reinsdorf said the hire was driven by his desire ‘‘to get better as fast as we possibly can’’ when it was clear the Sox were headed toward a rebuild. After all, they already had dealt several veteran players at the 2023 trade deadline.</p><p>Those criticisms only grew louder as the Sox got worse than anyone could have imagined before getting better. They lost a modern-record 121 games in 2024 as Getz’s early work as GM was focused on overhauling the infrastructure of the organization.</p><p>But behind the leadership of Getz, an overhauled front office and manager <b>Will Venable</b>, the Sox are headed to the American League Division Series.</p><p>By his own admission, it’s a year earlier than Reinsdorf anticipated watching his club celebrate a playoff-series victory.</p><p>‘‘It’s been gratifying to see these kids who believed in themselves when very few other people did believe in them,’’ Reinsdorf said. ‘‘The first thing I realized with Chris was the organization he was putting in place. When you build a building, the foundation comes first. He went about putting in place a terrific foundation, the scouting and minor-league development.”</p><p>Maybe building the Sox the right way means a bit more than finding the GM to do it through the right process. Or maybe sometimes you just know.</p><p>‘‘I felt in my bones [Getz] was the right guy,’’ Reinsdorf said.</p><h3>On to Cleveland</h3><p>The Sox won the season series against the Guardians, but it was by the slimmest of margins at 7-6. The Guardians claimed the AL Central title, taking the division lead after winning the last head-to-head matchup of the season and finishing one game ahead of the Sox.</p><p>A playoff showdown between the division foes seems only fitting.</p><p>‘‘It was kind of like it was already written,’’ shortstop <b>Colson Montgomery </b>said. ‘‘It came down to Cleveland in the regular season, and it’s going to come down to Cleveland right now. They’re a really good team, and we’re a really good team, too.”</p><p>The best-of-five series opens with two games in Cleveland and ensures at least one playoff game at Rate Field for the first time since the 2021 ALDS. But the Sox are aiming for a few more than that.</p><p>‘‘We expect to win,’’ Getz said.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/chicago-white-sox-manager-will-venable-general-manager-chris-getz-chairman-jerry-reinsdorf-jin-wong-houston-astros-cleveland-guardians-mlb-playoffs-postseason" >Will Venable deserves lots of credit for White Sox’ success, but he won’t take it</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/30/white-sox-keep-their-surprising-season-going-with-wild-card-series-sweep-in-houston-chase-meidroth-jerry-reinsdorf-chris-getz-will-venable-colson-montgomery-erick-fedde" >White Sox keep their surprising season going with wild-card series sweep in Houston</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
